children: Revenue rises nearly 20 per cent to Rs 31,998 crore in Q2 FY27, while first-half net profit more than triples to Rs 3,410 crore

State-owned Steel Authority of India or Sail reported a more than fourfold increase in standalone net profit to Rs 1,774 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 427 crore in the corresponding period last year. The sharp rise in profit was supported by higher sales volumes and cost optimisation measures.

Revenue from operations increased nearly 20 per cent year-on-year to Rs 31,998 crore during the quarter, against Rs 26,704 crore a year earlier. Net profit also rose 8.4 per cent sequentially from Rs 1,636 crore in the April-June quarter.
Sail chairman and managing director AK Panda said the company's financial performance reflected operational resilience and financial prudence amid volatility in global markets.

For the first half of FY27, Sail's standalone net profit more than tripled to Rs 3,410 crore from Rs 1,112 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) rose 55 per cent to Rs 8,917 crore during the April-September period, compared with Rs 5,754 crore a year earlier.

Sail's sales volumes increased 5.1 per cent year-on-year to 5.16 million tonnes in the September quarter, up from 4.91 million tonnes in the corresponding period last year. Crude steel production rose to 4.85 million tonnes from 4.65 million tonnes.

For the first half of FY27, however, sales volumes edged down to 9.33 million tonnes from 9.46 million tonnes in the year-ago period, even as profitability improved substantially. The company's outstanding debt stood at Rs 20,583 crore, reflecting its continued efforts to reduce borrowings and strengthen its balance sheet.

Panda said Sail would continue to focus on cost rationalisation, inventory reduction and increasing the share of high-end products. The company would also pursue a sustained reduction in borrowings to strengthen its financial position.
